mainTopic: The end of the כהן גדול's Torah reading on יום הכיפורים, his eight ברכות, the rest of his day's service in the משנה, and the dispute over when the מוסף offerings were brought.
overview: This amud finishes the rule about skipping during public reading: within תרי עשר you may skip, but not backward from the end of the book to its beginning. The גמרא then explains the כהן גדול's reading on יום הכיפורים. He rolls up the ספר תורה and announces that more is written in it, so no one thinks badly of the scroll. He recites ובעשור by heart because rolling the scroll would make the ציבור wait. He does not switch to a second scroll, either because people would suspect the first was flawed (רב הונא בר יהודה) or because it would cause an unnecessary ברכה (ריש לקיש). A ברייתא then lists his eight ברכות, and the גמרא explains that the משנה had to say watching the reading is not forbidden, because of ריש לקיש's rule אין מעבירין על המצות and the מצוה of ברב עם הדרת מלך. A new משנה describes the rest of his day: changing between gold and white garments, the rams and מוסף offerings (where רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא disagree), bringing out the כף and מחתה, the afternoon קטורת and lamps, and the celebration when he goes home. Finally, the גמרא asks how to read רבי עקיבא's words and when the פר העולה and אימורי חטאת were offered. רבא answers that the order is clear only in the דבי שמואל version of רבי אליעזר or the תוספתא version of רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The limit on skipping: not from the end of a book back to its start
steps.stepSummary: The skipping discussion ends with a limit: a reader may skip, but never from the end of the book back to its beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as he does not skip from the end of the book back to its beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the earlier ברייתא about skipping (לדלג) during public reading, here referring to skipping within תרי עשר. Skipping is allowed only if he does not jump backward from the end of the book to its start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line ends the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous amud: one may not skip from one prophet's book to another, but within תרי עשר (the Twelve Prophets, written as one book) one may skip. The limit here belongs to that rule: even within תרי עשר, you may not jump backward from the end of the book to its beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that / only on condition that
He will skip (from דִּלּוּג, skipping sections during reading)
Its beginning

phrases.english: Provided that he does not skip
phrases.notes: A limiting condition on the permission to skip.

phrases.english: from the end of the book to its beginning.
phrases.notes: Skipping backward across the whole book is excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the skipping discussion that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within תרי עשר one may skip, but not from the end of the book back to its beginning.

steps.title: Why does the כהן גדול announce that more is written?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about rolling the scroll and the announcement, and asks why all this is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He rolls the Torah scroll, etc.' Why is all this necessary?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the next line of the משנה. The כהן גדול rolls up the ספר תורה and says, 'More than what I read before you is written here.' The גמרא asks why he must make this announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'וכו׳' points to the rest of the משנה, which includes his statement to the crowd. The question is about purpose: why make a public declaration at all? This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolls / furls (a scroll)
Etc. (the rest of the quoted text)
And why all this? (asking for the purpose)

phrases.english: And he rolls the Torah scroll, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. It continues: he places it on his chest and says, 'More than what I read before you is written here.'

phrases.english: And why all this?
phrases.notes: Asks for the reason behind the announcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the skipping topic and moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the כהן גדול's announcement that more is written in the scroll.

steps.title: So people will not think badly of the ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The announcement prevents people from wrongly thinking the scroll is missing the portion he read by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: So as not to bring a bad name upon the Torah scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: he makes the announcement so that no one spreads a bad report (לעז) about the ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול will soon read a portion by heart. Onlookers might conclude that this portion is missing from the scroll, which would make the scroll seem פסול. The announcement protects the scroll's reputation.

keyTerms.meaning: To spread a bad report / cast aspersions
Torah scroll

phrases.english: so as not to spread a bad report
phrases.notes: Prevents people from suspecting something negative.

phrases.english: about the Torah scroll.
phrases.notes: They might think the portion read by heart is missing from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The announcement prevents people from suspecting the ספר תורה is incomplete.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול announces 'more is written here' to protect the honor of the ספר תורה, since he is about to read a portion by heart.

steps.title: The משנה: the ובעשור portion is read by heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the ובעשור portion from ספר במדבר is read by heart. This sets up the next question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The portion 'And on the tenth' from the book of Numbers, he reads by heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה: the כהן גדול recites the ובעשור section of ספר במדבר from memory. This quote is a setup for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two earlier readings, אחרי מות and אך בעשור, are both in ספר ויקרא, but ובעשור is in ספר במדבר, far away in the scroll. The משנה rules that he recites it by heart instead of reading it from the scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of Numbers (ספר במדבר), named for its census counts
By heart / from memory
'And on the tenth' (במדבר כ״ט:ז׳, the יום הכיפורים offerings)

phrases.english: 'And on the tenth' of the book of Numbers
phrases.notes: The section about the special offerings of יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: he reads by heart.
phrases.notes: Recited without the scroll.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶעָשׂוֹר שֶׁל חוֹמֶשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים קוֹרֵא עַל פֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ובעשור portion of ספר במדבר is recited by heart.

steps.title: Why not roll the scroll to that place and read it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: he could simply roll the scroll to ובעשור and read it properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let him roll the scroll and read!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the כהן גדול should recite by heart when he could roll the scroll forward to ספר במדבר and read from the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading from a written scroll is normally the proper way to read Torah in public. If that is possible here, reciting by heart seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what stops him.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let him roll and read

phrases.english: Why? Let him roll it and read!
phrases.notes: Proposes rolling the scroll to ספר במדבר instead of reciting by heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that ובעשור is read by heart.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading from the scroll is possible by rolling it, so reciting by heart seems unjustified.

steps.title: Rolling a scroll in public disrespects the community
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that one does not roll a ספר תורה in public, out of respect for the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said in the name of רב ששת: Because one does not roll a Torah scroll in public, out of respect for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that rolling the scroll from ספר ויקרא to ספר במדבר in front of everyone would make the ציבור sit and wait. That is a disgrace to them, so he recites by heart instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not that reading from the scroll is wrong. The problem is the long delay while rolling. כבוד הציבור outweighs the advantage of reading from the text.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not roll (a scroll)
In public / before the congregation
The honor of the community

steps.whyThisMatters: כבוד הציבור is a principle that shapes how Torah reading is run, for example by preparing the scroll before the reading starts.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said
phrases.notes: Attribution, first link in the chain.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
phrases.notes: The original author of the answer.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין גּוֹלְלִין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בְּצִיבּוּר,
phrases.english: because one does not roll a Torah scroll in public,
phrases.notes: Rolling far ahead takes time.

phrases.english: because of the honor of the community.
phrases.notes: Making them wait is disrespectful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies an overriding concern (כבוד הציבור) that blocks the proposed alternative.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could simply roll the scroll and read from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rolling in public makes the ציבור wait, which is disrespectful, so he recites by heart.

steps.title: Why not bring a second scroll already open to that place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: bring another ספר תורה already rolled to ובעשור, so no one waits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him bring another scroll and read from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If waiting is the problem, they could prepare a second ספר תורה already open to ובעשור and read from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes רב ששת's concern, since nobody has to wait. So reciting by heart again seems unnecessary, and the גמרא needs a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him bring
Another one

phrases.english: Let him bring another scroll and read!
phrases.notes: A second scroll, prepared in advance, avoids the delay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב ששת's reason fully explains reading by heart.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that he must read by heart.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second, pre-rolled scroll avoids the delay, so the reason of כבוד הציבור no longer applies.

steps.title: People would think the first scroll was flawed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה: switching to a second scroll would make people think the first one has a defect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said: Because of the disgrace of the first scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה answers that bringing a second scroll would make people suspect the first scroll was פגום, and that is why it was replaced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This concern resembles the earlier worry about לעז: protecting the reputation of a ספר תורה. Switching scrolls in the middle sends a misleading message about the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: Its flaw / its disgrace
The first (scroll)

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: First answer.

phrases.english: because of the disgrace of the first one.
phrases.notes: People would assume the first scroll was found פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new concern that blocks the second-scroll option.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second scroll solves the waiting problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second scroll would imply the first scroll was flawed.

steps.title: A second scroll would cause an unnecessary blessing
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different reason: a new scroll would require an extra ברכה, which is a ברכה שאינה צריכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: Because of a blessing that is not necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers differently. Reading from a new scroll would require new ברכות, and that would be a ברכה שאינה צריכה. Reciting by heart avoids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second, independent answer to the same challenge. רב הונא בר יהודה focuses on the scroll's honor, while ריש לקיש focuses on avoiding an unnecessary ברכה. Either way, the conclusion is the same: he recites by heart.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnecessary blessing
The אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש

steps.whatToRemember: He recites ובעשור by heart because of three concerns. Rolling the scroll makes the ציבור wait (כבוד הציבור). Bringing a second scroll either disgraces the first scroll (רב הונא בר יהודה) or causes a ברכה שאינה צריכה (ריש לקיש).

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
phrases.notes: An alternative answer.

phrases.english: because of a blessing that is not necessary.
phrases.notes: A new scroll would require repeating the Torah-reading ברכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel answer to the same challenge that step 8 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative concern that blocks the second-scroll option.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second scroll solves the waiting problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second scroll would require an extra, unnecessary ברכה.

steps.title: Challenge from the three scrolls of ראש חודש טבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we really worry about פגם, since רבי יצחק נפחא rules that three ספרי תורה are used when ראש חודש טבת falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really worry that people will think a scroll is flawed? Didn't רבי יצחק נפחא say: When ראש חודש טבת falls on שבת, we bring three Torah scrolls. We read from one the portion of the day, from one the portion of ראש חודש, and from one the portion of חנוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא בר יהודה's answer from step 8. It brings a case where we use several scrolls and do not worry that people will suspect a defect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר יהודה said a second scroll makes people think the first one is flawed. But on ראש חודש טבת that falls on שבת, three different scrolls are taken out. If switching scrolls caused suspicion of פגם, this practice should be a problem too.

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned / we worry
a flaw or defect (the suspicion that the scroll is invalid)
the new month of טבת, which always falls during חנוכה
the regular portion of the day (the weekly פרשה)

phrases.english: And are we really concerned about a flaw?
phrases.notes: Targets רב הונא בר יהודה's reason in step 8.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha say:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ טֵבֵת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.english: When Rosh Chodesh Tevet falls on Shabbat
we bring three Torah scrolls
and we read from one the portion of the day,
and from one the portion of Rosh Chodesh,
and from one the portion of Chanukah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason of רב הונא בר יהודה given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר יהודה's claim that using a second scroll causes suspicion of פגם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Common practice uses three scrolls on one day without worrying about פגם, so the worry seems baseless.

steps.title: Three readers are different from one reader switching scrolls
steps.stepSummary: Three people reading from three scrolls raises no suspicion. One person switching between two scrolls does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three men reading from three scrolls: there is no suspicion of a flaw. One man reading from two scrolls: there is a suspicion of a flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא בר יהודה by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש חודש טבת each scroll goes to a different reader, so people assume each reading simply gets its own scroll. When the כהן גדול himself drops one scroll and picks up another, people will wonder what was wrong with the first one. So the worry about פגם still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: men (here: the people called up to read)
scrolls
there is not / there is

steps.whatToRemember: The worry about פגם only applies when one reader switches scrolls in the middle, not when different readers each use their own scroll.

phrases.english: Three men with three scrolls —
there is no suspicion of a flaw,
one man with two scrolls —
there is a suspicion of a flaw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (חילוק: three readers vs. one reader)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of more than one scroll makes people suspect פגם, so the three-scroll practice disproves the worry.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suspicion arises only when a single reader switches scrolls. Separate readers with separate scrolls raise no suspicion.

steps.title: The eight blessings of the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'eight ברכות' and brings a ברייתא that lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he recites eight blessings over it.' The Rabbis taught: about the Torah, the way it is said in the synagogue; about the Temple service, about thanksgiving, and about forgiveness of sin, in their usual form; about the מקדש on its own; about the כהנים on their own; about ישראל on its own; and about the rest of the prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה, which says the כהן גדול recites eight ברכות. It brings a ברייתא that names each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the eight: a ברכת התורה, three ברכות taken from the regular תפילה (עבודה, הודאה, מחילה), and four special ones for the מקדש, the כהנים, ישראל, and a general closing prayer. 'כתיקנה' means the three regular ones keep their usual wording. 'בפני עצמו' means each of the last ones is its own separate ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: eight blessings
the Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
the Temple service (the ברכה of רצה)
thanksgiving (the ברכה of מודים)
according to its set, usual wording
on its own, as a separate blessing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count 'על העבודה ועל ההודאה ועל מחילת העון' as one ברכה. They are three separate ברכות, which brings the total to eight.

phrases.english: 'And he recites eight blessings over it.'
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
About the Torah —
the way one blesses in the synagogue,
about the Temple service, and about thanksgiving,
and about forgiveness of sin, in their set form.
And about the Temple on its own,
and about the priests on their own,
and about Israel on its own,
and about the rest of the prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְבָרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ שְׁמוֹנֶה בְּרָכוֹת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of rolling and switching scrolls and explains the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eight ברכות are: Torah, עבודה, הודאה, מחילת העון, מקדש, כהנים, ישראל, and שאר תפילה.

steps.title: The wording of the final blessing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the text of the 'rest of the prayer' ברכה and its closing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The rest of the prayer is: 'Song, supplication, and request before You for Your people ישראל, who need to be saved.' And he ends with 'Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא explains what the eighth ברכה, 'the rest of the prayer,' actually says and how it ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last ברכה is a general plea for כלל ישראל to be saved. It ends with the familiar חתימה 'שומע תפילה', the same closing as in our weekday שמונה עשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: song, supplication, request
to be saved
and he concludes (the closing line of a ברכה)
Who hears prayer

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
And the rest of the prayer is:
'Song, supplication, request before You
for Your people Israel, who need to be saved'
and he concludes with 'Who hears prayer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the eighth ברכה from the list in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'rest of the prayer' ברכה asks for the salvation of ישראל and ends with 'שומע תפילה'.

steps.title: Everyone reads from his own scroll
steps.stepSummary: After the כהן גדול finishes, each person brings a ספר תורה from home and reads from it to show its beauty to the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And afterward, each and every person brings a Torah scroll from his house and reads from it, in order to show its beauty to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues. It describes what happens after the כהן גדול's reading and ברכות are done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the official reading is over, individuals take out their own ספרי תורה and read from them. The stated reason is to display the scroll's beautiful appearance in public, a form of honoring the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: each and every one
from his house
its appearance / beauty
to the public

steps.whatToRemember: After the official reading and its eight ברכות, each person reads from his own beautiful ספר תורה to honor the Torah in public.

phrases.english: And afterward,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵבִיא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מִבֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: each and every one brings a Torah scroll from his house,
and reads from it
in order to show its beauty to the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחַר כָּךְ, כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵבִיא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מִבֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with what happens after the ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person reads from his own ספר תורה afterward to display its beauty publicly.

steps.title: Why did the משנה need to say it is not forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that watching both events is 'not because one is not permitted.' It asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who sees the כהן גדול reading, etc., does not see the burning, and this is not because he is not allowed.' The גמרא asks: that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and challenges it as unnecessary. This sets up the next step, which will explain why the line was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explained that a person can't see both events because they happen at the same time in different places. Adding 'it's not forbidden' seems pointless, because what prohibition could there be in watching? The גמרא wants to know why the משנה bothered to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sees / watches
Permitted, allowed
It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement is unnecessary)

phrases.english: One who sees the High Priest, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה. The 'etc.' points to: 'does not see the פר and שעיר being burned.'

phrases.english: not because he is not permitted.
phrases.notes: The משנה's reason is distance and timing, not a prohibition.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The challenge: why would anyone think it was forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to an earlier line of the משנה, after the discussion of people reading from their own ספרי תורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'לא מפני שאינו רשאי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no clear reason to forbid watching both events, so saying it is not forbidden seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought it was forbidden because of ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needed to say it, because we might have applied ריש לקיש's rule that one does not pass over a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said it is forbidden, following ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש said: one does not pass over מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Without the משנה's words, we might have thought ריש לקיש's rule forbids leaving the reading to go watch the burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש teaches that when a מצוה is in front of you, you should not skip it to go to another one. If the person is already at the reading, leaving it to see the burning could look like skipping a מצוה. The משנה tells us the real issue is only practical, not a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
The אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש
One does not pass over מצוות

steps.whyThisMatters: אין מעבירין על המצות is a well-known halachic principle that is used in many places across ש״ס.

phrases.english: You might have said it is like Reish Lakish's view.
For Reish Lakish said:
One does not pass over מצוות.
phrases.notes: Once you are at one מצוה, do not skip it for another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement prevents a reasonable mistake (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving the reading to watch the burning might be forbidden under אין מעבירין על המצות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not forbidden. One simply cannot be in both places at once.

steps.title: What מצוה is there in watching the reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מצוה is involved in being at the כהן גדול's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what מצוה is there here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the previous answer. It sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule only applies if there is a מצוה being passed over. Simply watching the כהן גדול read does not seem to be a מצוה. So the גמרא asks which מצוה it is.

keyTerms.meaning: And what מצוה is it?

phrases.english: And what מצוה is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the premise of the תירוץ in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מצוה makes watching the reading something one should not pass over.

steps.title: The מצוה of a large crowd honoring the King
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה is ברב עם הדרת מלך, so the משנה had to teach that leaving it is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה is 'In a multitude of people is the King's glory.' So the משנה comes to teach us that it is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the מצוה: a big crowd at a מצוה gives honor to ה׳. It then closes the discussion with 'קא משמע לן,' meaning this is what the משנה came to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because being part of the crowd is a real מצוה, we might have thought you may not leave it. The משנה therefore had to state clearly that the only problem is distance and timing. That is why its words 'not because he is not permitted' are not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: In a multitude of people is the King's glory (משלי יד:כח)
It teaches us (this is the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's words 'not because he is not permitted' are needed. Otherwise we would think ריש לקיש's rule forbids leaving the מצוה of ברב עם הדרת מלך.

phrases.english: "In the multitude of people is the King's glory,"
phrases.notes: משלי יד:כח. A large gathering honors ה׳.

phrases.english: it teaches us.
phrases.notes: The משנה teaches that it is still not forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and closes the discussion that began in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצוה is ברב עם הדרת מלך, so the משנה had to tell us that leaving it is not forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Watching the reading is a מצוה, yet missing the burning (or the reading) is only a practical matter, not a prohibition.

steps.title: The כהן גדול changes back into the golden garments
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: after reading in linen, the כהן גדול washes, removes the linen, immerses, dries, puts on gold garments, and washes again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he read in the linen garments, he washed his hands and feet. He took off the linen, went down and immersed, came up and dried himself. They brought him the golden garments, he put them on, and he washed his hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and describes the כהן גדול's change of clothing after the Torah reading. This prepares for the remaining offerings of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every change of garments on יום כיפור requires washing hands and feet before and after, with an immersion in between. Here he switches from the white linen garments to the golden garments. He needs the golden garments for the next offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
White linen garments, worn for the special יום כיפור service
Washing hands and feet from the כיור
Immersion in a מקוה
The golden garments of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he read in the linen garments,
phrases.notes: The משנה earlier allowed him to read in linen or in his own white robe.

phrases.english: he sanctified his hands and feet.
phrases.notes: Washing before removing the garments.

phrases.english: He removed them, went down and immersed,
came up and dried himself,
and they brought him golden garments and he put them on,
and he sanctified his hands and feet,
phrases.notes: Washing after putting on the new garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה continuing the order of the יום כיפור service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the reading, the כהן גדול changes from linen to gold with washing, immersion, and washing again.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the rams and seven lambs are offered now
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אליעזר, the כהן גדול now offers his ram, the people's ram, and the seven lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out and offered his ram, the ram of the people, and the seven perfect one-year-old lambs. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states רבי אליעזר's view of what is offered right after the change into gold garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rams are עולות from ויקרא טז. The seven lambs are part of the מוסף from במדבר כט. רבי אליעזר places all of them at this point, after the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: His (the כהן גדול's) ram, an עולה
The ram of the people, an עולה
Seven lambs of the מוסף

phrases.english: and he went out and offered his ram
and the ram of the people

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שִׁבְעַת כְּבָשִׂים תְּמִימִים בְּנֵי שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: and the seven unblemished year-old lambs,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with what the כהן גדול does in the golden garments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the two rams and seven lambs are offered after the reading.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: these were offered with the morning and afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the seven lambs came with the morning תמיד. The מוסף bull and outer goat came with the afternoon תמיד, though the גמרא will question where the bull belongs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: they were offered with the morning תמיד. And the bull of the עולה and the goat that is done outside were offered with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי עקיבא, who disagrees with רבי אליעזר about the timing of these offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא agrees that the two rams come after the reading. However, he moves the seven lambs to the start of the day, with the morning תמיד. He then mentions the מוסף bull and the מוסף חטאת goat with the afternoon תמיד, though the גמרא (steps 26–27) asks whether the bull really belongs with the afternoon group. The goat is called 'done outside' to separate it from the inner goat whose blood was brought into the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily morning offering
The daily afternoon offering
The bull brought as an עולה for מוסף
The מוסף goat offered in the courtyard (outside)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'the goat done outside' with the שעיר לעזאזל or the inner goat. It is the מוסף חטאת goat, which is offered on the outer מזבח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר places the rams and the seven lambs after the reading. רבי עקיבא places the seven lambs with the morning תמיד and the מוסף bull and goat with the afternoon תמיד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיוּ קְרֵבִין.
phrases.english: they were offered with the morning daily offering.
phrases.notes: Refers to the seven lambs (as the גמרא reads it in step 26).

phrases.english: And the bull of the burnt-offering and the goat performed outside —

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ קְרֵבִין עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם.
phrases.english: were offered with the afternoon daily offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: the seven lambs come with the morning תמיד, while the מוסף bull and outer goat come with the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: He removes the gold garments and immerses again
steps.stepSummary: After the offerings he finished in gold garments, the כהן גדול washes his hands and feet, takes off the gold garments, immerses, comes up, and dries himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He washed his hands and feet and took off the gold clothes. Then he went down into the מקוה, immersed, came up, and dried himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the order of the day. Now that the offerings done in gold garments are finished, the כהן גדול gets ready to change clothes again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern we saw before: wash, take off, immerse, dry. Here it closes the gold-garment section of the day. It prepares him to put the white garments back on in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He washed (sanctified) his hands and feet from the כִּיּוֹר (the washing basin)
He took off (his garments)
He immersed in a מִקְוֶה
He dried himself off with a towel

phrases.english: He sanctified his hands and feet and removed (the gold garments),
phrases.notes: The washing comes before taking off the garments, as it is done when leaving one set of garments.

phrases.english: and he went down, immersed, came up, and dried himself.
phrases.notes: This immersion took place in a מקוה in the Temple area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה right after the offerings in gold garments described in steps 19–21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the gold-garment offerings, the כהן גדול washes his hands and feet, removes the garments, immerses, and dries off.

steps.title: Back in white garments to remove the spoon and coal pan
steps.stepSummary: He puts on white garments, washes his hands and feet, and enters the קודש הקדשים to bring out the כף and the מחתה. Then he washes, removes the white garments, immerses, and dries off.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him white clothes and he put them on, and washed his hands and feet. He went in to take out the spoon and the coal pan. Then he washed his hands and feet, took off the clothes, went down, immersed, came up, and dried himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The כהן גדול goes back into the קודש הקדשים one more time, just to bring out the כף and מחתה he left there earlier in the day. This must be done in white garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, he brought the קטורת into the קודש הקדשים with a כף (spoon) and a מחתה (coal pan), and they stayed inside. Anything done inside the קודש הקדשים is done in white garments, so he must change back into them for this. Once finished, he goes through the full cycle again: wash, remove, immerse, dry.

keyTerms.meaning: White linen garments worn for the special יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים service inside
The spoon (ladle) that held the קְטֹרֶת
The coal pan that held the burning coals
The Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he is offering more קטורת here. This entry is only to bring out the utensils left behind from the קטורת he offered in the קודש הקדשים earlier in the day.

phrases.english: They brought him white garments and he put them on,
and he sanctified his hands and feet.
phrases.notes: This washing is for putting on the new garments.

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנַס לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה.
phrases.english: He entered (the קודש הקדשים) to take out the spoon and the coal pan.
phrases.notes: These were left inside from when he offered the קטורת earlier.

phrases.english: He sanctified his hands and feet and removed (the white garments),
and he went down, immersed, came up, and dried himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having taken off the gold garments in step 22, he now puts on white garments for the next task.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing the כף and מחתה from the קודש הקדשים is done in white garments, surrounded by washings and an immersion.

steps.title: Gold garments for the afternoon incense and the lamps
steps.stepSummary: He puts on gold garments, washes, and enters the היכל to offer the afternoon קטורת and tend the lamps of the מנורה. Then he washes, removes the gold garments, immerses, and dries off.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him gold clothes and he put them on, and washed his hands and feet. He went in to burn the afternoon incense and to tend the lamps. Then he washed his hands and feet, took off the clothes, went down, immersed, came up, and dried himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The כהן גדול now does the regular daily afternoon jobs, the same ones done every day of the year. Because they are regular jobs, he wears the gold garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every day there is קטורת offered in the afternoon and the lamps of the מנורה are tended. On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול does these himself. Since they are ordinary daily services, they are done in gold garments, not white. These are the last services of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: The eight golden garments the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל wears all year
The regular afternoon incense offered every day
Tending (preparing/lighting) the lamps of the מְנוֹרָה
The Sanctuary room containing the מְנוֹרָה and the incense altar

steps.confusionAlert: This קטורת is not the special קטורת of the קודש הקדשים. It is the regular daily afternoon קטורת offered on the inner golden altar in the היכל.

phrases.english: They brought him gold garments and he put them on,
and he sanctified his hands and feet,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִכְנַס לְהַקְטִיר קְטוֹרֶת שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם,
phrases.english: and he entered (the היכל) to burn the afternoon incense,
and to tend the lamps,
phrases.notes: In the afternoon, tending the lamps means preparing and lighting them for the night.

phrases.english: and he sanctified his hands and feet and removed (the gold garments),
and he went down, immersed, came up, and dried himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the white-garment task in step 23, he changes to gold garments for the final daily services.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The afternoon קטורת and tending of the lamps are done by the כהן גדול in gold garments, ending the day's עבודה.

steps.title: He goes home in his own clothes and celebrates
steps.stepSummary: He puts on his own clothes, the people escort him home, and he makes a celebration for his friends because he came out of the קודש safely.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him his own clothes and he put them on, and they escort him to his house. He would make a celebration for his loved ones when he left the holy place in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The עבודה of the day is done. The כהן גדול puts on his regular clothes, the people walk him home with honor, and he throws a celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Entering the קודש הקדשים was dangerous; a כהן גדול who was not worthy could die there. So when he came out alive and well, it was a real reason to celebrate. The escort home shows the people's honor for him.

keyTerms.meaning: His own personal (non-priestly) clothes
They escort him (as a sign of honor)
Here: a festive celebration or feast
His friends and loved ones

steps.whatToRemember: The day of the כהן גדול follows a fixed pattern: every change of clothing is surrounded by washing hands and feet and an immersion. White garments are for the special inner services of יום הכיפורים (including bringing out the כף and מחתה), and gold garments are for the regular daily services. The day ends with him going home in his own clothes and celebrating his safe exit.
steps.whyThisMatters: The celebration reminds us how serious and dangerous the service in the קודש הקדשים was. Coming out safely was seen as a sign that the עבודה was accepted.

phrases.english: They brought him his own clothes and he put them on,
and they escort him to his house.
And he would make a celebration for his loved ones
at the time that he left the holy place in peace.
phrases.notes: Coming out safely from the קודש הקדשים showed his service was accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the final immersion in step 24, he leaves the priestly garments behind and goes home, ending the day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the end of the day the כהן גדול wears his own clothes, is escorted home, and makes a celebration for his safe exit from the קודש.

steps.title: How should רבי עקיבא's sentence be read? First possibility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read רבי עקיבא's words. One option is that פר העולה and the outer שעיר were both offered with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked: What exactly is he saying? Is it this: 'With the morning תמיד they were offered,' and then the burnt-offering bull and the goat done outside were offered with the afternoon תמיד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a question about the משנה. It suggests the first of two ways to read רבי עקיבא's sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's sentence is ambiguous because it is unclear which group פר העולה belongs to. In this first reading, the words 'פר העולה ושעיר הנעשה בחוץ' are one unit, and both animals were offered in the afternoon. This matches the way the משנה summary in step 21 was understood.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)
How is he saying it? What does he mean?
The burnt-offering bull of the יום הכפורים מוסף
The מוסף goat whose service is done outside, in the courtyard
The daily afternoon offering

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different goats on יום הכפורים. The 'goat done outside' is the מוסף goat offered in the courtyard. It is NOT the goat whose blood is brought inside the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: How is he saying it?
phrases.notes: Asking about רבי עקיבא's wording

phrases.aramaic: עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיוּ קְרֵבִין,
phrases.english: 'With the morning תמיד they were offered,'
phrases.notes: Refers to the seven lambs

phrases.english: and the burnt-offering bull and the goat done outside
phrases.notes: In this reading the two are one group

phrases.english: were offered with the afternoon תמיד?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the description of the כהן גדול's day to analyze the wording of רבי עקיבא's statement in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does פר העולה belong with the afternoon group or with the morning group in רבי עקיבא's statement?

steps.title: How should רבי עקיבא's sentence be read? Second possibility
steps.stepSummary: The second option is that פר העולה went with the morning lambs, and only the outer שעיר was offered in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps this is what he is saying: 'With the morning תמיד they were offered,' and the burnt-offering bull together with them. And the goat done outside was offered with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. Maybe the bull belongs with the morning group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word 'and' before פר העולה joins the bull to the earlier clause, the morning lambs. In this reading, only the outer goat waits until the afternoon. רבא's answer in step 30 and the תוספתא quoted in step 32 settle this question.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps
This is what he is saying
Together with them

phrases.english: Or perhaps this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: Introduces the second side of the question

phrases.aramaic: עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיוּ קְרֵבִין,
phrases.english: 'With the morning תמיד they were offered,'
and the burnt-offering bull together with them,
phrases.notes: The bull joins the morning group

phrases.english: and the goat done outside
was offered with the afternoon תמיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the bull is joined to the morning clause instead of the afternoon clause.

steps.title: When does רבי אליעזר say the bull was offered?
steps.stepSummary: A second question: רבי אליעזר left פר העולה out of his list, so when does he hold it was offered?
steps.simpleTranslation: And another question: According to רבי אליעזר, who left out the burnt-offering bull, when does the כהן גדול offer it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new question. רבי אליעזר's list in the משנה does not mention the bull, so his timing for it is unknown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר named the rams and the seven lambs but said nothing about פר העולה. Every מוסף offering must be brought at some point, so the גמרא asks when he places the bull in the day's order. This second question is added before the first one is answered. Both are resolved in steps 30–32.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another question)
Since he left it out
When does he perform it?

phrases.english: And furthermore: the burnt-offering bull, according to רבי אליעזר,
since he left it out, when does he perform it?
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר's list in the משנה omits the bull

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: פַּר הָעוֹלָה לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּשַׁיְּירֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate question to the chain using וְתוּ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what point in the day does רבי אליעזר hold the כהן גדול offers פר העולה?

steps.title: When were the sin-offering fats burned, according to both opinions?
steps.stepSummary: A third question: neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי עקיבא mentioned the אימורי חטאת, so when were they placed on the altar?
steps.simpleTranslation: And another question: Both according to רבי אליעזר and according to רבי עקיבא, when does he offer the sacrificial parts of the sin-offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third question that applies to both תנאים. Neither one said when the fats of the sin-offerings go on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin-offerings of the day include the inner bull and goat. Certain parts of them, called the אימורים, must be burned on the outer altar. The משנה's order does not say when this happens, so the גמרא asks about it. All three questions are now waiting for answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of the sin-offering that are burned on the altar

keyTerms.term: בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֵּין לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
keyTerms.meaning: Both according to רבי אליעזר and according to רבי עקיבא

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has opened three questions: (1) whether רבי עקיבא puts פר העולה in the morning or the afternoon, (2) when רבי אליעזר places פר העולה, and (3) when both תנאים place the אימורי חטאת. The answers come next.

phrases.english: And furthermore: both according to רבי אליעזר
and according to רבי עקיבא,
the parts of the sin-offering, when does he perform them?
phrases.notes: Neither תנא mentioned them in the משנה

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֵּין לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third question to the chain, now covering both opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When in the day's order are the אימורי חטאת placed on the altar, according to both תנאים?

steps.title: רבא: The order only works in two other versions
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the order of offerings cannot be explained neatly using the version we had. It only fits according to רבי אליעזר as taught in דבי שמואל, or רבי עקיבא as taught in the תוספתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You will not find a properly arranged order, except either according to רבי אליעזר as taught in the school of שמואל, or according to רבי עקיבא as taught in the תוספתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the three open questions by saying the version we had cannot be lined up. The גמרא is setting up to quote two other versions that give a complete order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not try to patch the old version. He points to two other sources that already contain a full, clean order. The next two steps quote those sources.

keyTerms.meaning: Properly arranged; a neat, consistent order
The school of שמואל, which taught its own collection of ברייתות
A collection of teachings from the time of the משנה, outside the משנה itself

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying רבי אליעזר or רבי עקיבא made a mistake. He is saying the wording we had is unclear. Other versions of their same opinions give the order cleanly.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You will not find it properly arranged,
except either according to Rabbi Eliezer
as taught in the school of Shmuel,
or according to Rabbi Akiva as in the Tosefta.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ מְתַקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions raised in steps 26–29 about gaps in the order of offerings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A neat order exists only in the דבי שמואל version of רבי אליעזר or the תוספתא version of רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's full order in the school of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: In the דבי שמואל version, רבי אליעזר says: after coming out, the כהן גדול offered his ram, the people's ram, and the אימורי חטאת. The פר העולה, the seven lambs, and the outer שעיר were offered with the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of שמואל taught: רבי אליעזר says: He came out and offered his ram, the ram of the people, and the sacrificial portions of the sin-offering. But the bull of the burnt-offering, the seven lambs, and the goat that is done outside are offered with the afternoon daily offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first clean source that רבא pointed to. This is רבי אליעזר's opinion as taught in דבי שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version fills both gaps from before. It names the פר העולה and places it in the afternoon. It also places the אימורי חטאת right after the two rams. So רבי אליעזר's order is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram of the people, brought as an עולה for all of ישראל
The fats and parts of the חטאת that are burned on the altar
The seven lambs of the מוסף of יום כיפור
The outer goat: the מוסף חטאת offered on the outer altar, not the inner goat whose blood goes into the קודש הקדשים
The daily afternoon offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers both the question of when פר העולה was offered according to רבי אליעזר (step 28) and the question about the אימורי חטאת (step 29).

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As the school of Shmuel taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
He came out and offered his ram and the ram of the people
and the sacrificial portions of the sin-offering,
but the bull of the burnt-offering and the seven lambs
and the goat that is done outside —
are offered with the afternoon daily offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first of the two sources that רבא named.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר: the two rams and the אימורי חטאת come right after he comes out. פר העולה, the seven lambs, and the outer שעיר come with the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's order in the תוספתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תוספתא version of רבי עקיבא says. It quotes it: פר העולה and the seven lambs were offered with the morning תמיד, based on a פסוק. Only after that came the special service of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the תוספתא of רבי עקיבא? As it was taught: רבי עקיבא says: The bull of the burnt-offering and the seven lambs were offered with the morning daily offering. As it says: 'Besides the morning burnt-offering which is for the daily burnt-offering.' And afterward comes the service of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the wording of the second source רבא mentioned, then quotes it. It is רבי עקיבא's opinion as found in the תוספתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version settles the question from step 27. It clearly puts פר העולה together with the seven lambs in the morning. The פסוק links the מוסף offerings to the morning תמיד. The special יום כיפור service only starts after that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to quote the source being referred to
The daily morning offering
Besides the morning burnt-offering. The פסוק linking the מוסף to the morning תמיד
The special יום כיפור service done by the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: the order of offerings is clear only in two versions. In רבי אליעזר's version (from דבי שמואל), פר העולה, the seven lambs, and the outer שעיר come in the afternoon. In רבי עקיבא's version (from the תוספתא), פר העולה and the seven lambs come in the morning with the תמיד, before עבודת היום.

phrases.english: What is the Tosefta of Rabbi Akiva?
As it was taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
The bull of the burnt-offering and the seven lambs

phrases.aramaic: עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיוּ קְרֵבִין,
phrases.english: were offered with the morning daily offering,
as it is said: 'Besides the morning burnt-offering
which is for the daily burnt-offering,'
and afterward the service of the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the second source that רבא named, after the רבי אליעזר source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא: פר העולה and the seven lambs are offered with the morning תמיד, before עבודת היום, based on 'מלבד עולת הבקר.'
